headline: Wider and constrained search spaces reshape peptide and modification identification
label: Proteomics Search Space Expansion
summary: Recent tools widen or constrain search spaces for PTMs, proteoforms, and modified RNA, with new evidence on peptide coverage bias.
synthesis: The dominant thread is how search spaces are widened or constrained, and how the resulting assignments are then tested. MS Andrea scores combinations of PTMs per PSM in open searches using sequence tags and MS Amanda scoring, outperforming MSFragger and Sage. OligoFragger constrains modified-oligonucleotide searches with MS/MS fragment evidence, improving FDR-controlled identification. mE-DIA combines multi-enzyme, library-free DIA-MS with proteoform inference and reports a 30% increase in protein identifications. SeekNSee applies enzyme-aware in silico digestion and traceable rule-level scoring to prioritize proteotypic peptides. A reanalysis of public bottom-up proteomics data finds basic-pI peptides depleted (OR 0.45), indicating systematic coverage bias. What is new is the shift toward proteoform-level resolution and explicit measurement of coverage gaps, with search constraints and scoring rules made traceable.
